concept_explanation: A function is a special type of relation where each element x in set X (domain) is mapped to exactly one element y in set Y (codomain). This is often represented as f: x → y or y = f(x). For example, the linear function y = 2x + 1 maps each x to a unique y. Functions can be represented graphically, where each x-value corresponds to a single point on the graph, or using arrow diagrams.
common_mistakes: A common mistake is to think that any relation is a function. Remember: a function requires each input to have exactly one output.

concept_explanation: A function is a special relation that maps each object (input) from the domain to exactly one image (output) in the codomain. The function notation f: x → y or f(x) = y is used, where x is the object and y is the image. For example, if f: x → 2x + 1, then f(1)=3, f(3)=7, f(5)=11. A function must satisfy the condition that every object has only one image; it can be one-to-one or many-to-one.
worked_example: Example 1: Determine whether each relation is a function. (a) Mapping: 2→8, 5→20, 6→24 (each 1 object, 1 image) → function. (b) Mapping: 4→2, 8→3, 8→9 (object 8 has two images) → not a function. (c) Mapping: 1→a, 3→a, 9→c (one-to-many? actually 1→a,3→a is many-to-one? Wait, 1 and 3 both go to a, 9→c, that's many-to-one, each object has one image, so function). (d) Mapping: a→4, b→10, b→7, c→12 (b has two images) → not a function.
common_mistakes: A common mistake is thinking that a mapping where an object has two outputs is still a function. In a function, each object must map to exactly one image.

concept_explanation: The vertical line test determines whether a graph represents a function. If any vertical line drawn on the graph intersects it at more than one point, then the relation is not a function. If every vertical line intersects the graph at most once (including zero intersections for x-values not in the domain), then the relation is a function. This test checks that each x-value in the domain is paired with exactly one y-value.
worked_example: Example 2: (a) The graph is a function because a vertical line cuts at only one point, except at x=1 where it does not intersect (x=1 is not in the domain, so it does not violate the rule). (b) The graph is a function because a vertical line always cuts at only one point. (c) The graph is not a function because a vertical line cuts at two points (e.g., at x=0, it intersects twice).
common_mistakes: A common mistake is to think that if a vertical line does not intersect the graph at all, then the graph is not a function. However, zero intersections simply mean that the x-value is not in the domain, which is allowed; the function only requires that for each x in the domain, there is exactly one y.

concept_explanation: The absolute value function is defined as f(x) = |x|, where |x| represents the numerical value of x. It is piecewise defined: |x| = x when x ≥ 0, and |x| = -x when x < 0. The graph of f(x) = |x| is V-shaped with vertex at (0,0), and the function always outputs non-negative values.
common_mistakes: Students often incorrectly think |x| equals ±x or forget that absolute value yields only non-negative values. Another mistake is misapplying the piecewise definition when x is negative.

subtopic: Menentukan domain dan julat bagi suatu fungsi
concept_explanation: Domain bagi suatu fungsi ialah set semua nilai input yang mungkin, manakala julat ialah set semua nilai output yang terhasil. Fungsi boleh diskret (nilai input terhad) atau selanjar (nilai input dalam selang). Contohnya, fungsi y = 18x bagi bilangan tiket x dari 1 hingga 5 mempunyai domain {1,2,3,4,5} dan julat {18,36,54,72,90}.
worked_example: Situasi I: Fungsi y = 18x mewakili harga tiket (RM) bagi x tiket. Lukis graf untuk x = 1 hingga 5. Domain: {1,2,3,4,5}. Julat: {18,36,54,72,90}.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa ialah menganggap domain dan julat sentiasa semua nombor nyata, padahal bagi fungsi diskret domain adalah terhad kepada nilai-nilai tertentu.

concept_explanation: A discrete function consists of isolated points that are not connected by a line or curve, while a continuous function has points connected by a straight line or curve within a given interval. The domain is the set of all possible input values (x) for which the function is defined, and the range is the set of all output values (y) obtained from substituting the domain values. For example, in a mapping diagram, the elements in set X form the domain, and the corresponding elements in set Y form the range.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse discrete and continuous functions by thinking that all functions with points plotted on a graph are discrete. They also incorrectly identify the domain as all x-values in the entire coordinate plane instead of only the given set or interval.

concept_explanation: Domain is the set of all possible input values (x) of a function. Codomain is the set of all possible output values (y) that the function can theoretically produce, while range is the set of actual outputs produced by the domain. For example, in an arrow diagram, domain is the set of first elements, codomain is the set of second elements, and range is the subset of codomain that has incoming arrows. For a continuous function, domain and range are intervals.
worked_example: Example 5: Function f is defined as f : x → |2x – 1|. Sketch the graph of f in the domain –1 < x < 2 and state the range. Solution: Create a table for x values –1, 0, 0.5, 1, 2. Compute f(x) = |2x – 1|: when x = –1, f(x) = 3; x = 0, f(x) = 1; x = 0.5, f(x) = 0; x = 1, f(x) = 1; x = 2, f(x) = 3. Plot points (–1,3), (0,1), (0.5,0), (1,1), (2,3). The graph is V-shaped with vertex at (0.5,0). The range is { y : 0 ≤ y ≤ 3 }.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse codomain with range. Range is always a subset of codomain. Also, when sketching absolute value functions, mistakes occur in reflecting negative parts of the graph.

subtopic: Determining the image of a function when the object is given and vice versa
concept_explanation: In a function, the object (input, x) is mapped to its image (output, f(x)). Given an object, substitute it into the function rule to find the image. Conversely, given an image, set f(x) equal to that value and solve for x. Domain restrictions (e.g., x ≠ 0) must be observed to avoid undefined values.
worked_example:
Example 6: Function f is defined by f : x → 3x + 5/x, x ≠ 0. (a) Find f(5). (b) Find the image of 1/3 under f. (c) Find the possible values of x when their image is 8.
Solution:
(a) f(5) = 3(5) + 5/5 = 15 + 1 = 16.
(b) f(1/3) = 3(1/3) + 5/(1/3) = 1 + 15 = 16.
(c) f(x) = 8 → 3x + 5/x = 8. Multiply both sides by x: 3x² + 5 = 8x → 3x² - 8x + 5 = 0 → (3x - 5)(x - 1) = 0 → x = 5/3 or x = 1.
common_mistakes: Forgetting domain restrictions (e.g., x ≠ 0) when solving for the object, which can lead to including invalid or undefined values.

concept_title: Solving Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
concept_explanation: The absolute value function f(x) = |ax - b| represents the distance of ax - b from zero. To solve |ax - b| = k, consider both cases: ax - b = k and ax - b = -k. For inequalities, |ax - b| < k implies -k < ax - b < k, while |ax - b| > k implies ax - b < -k or ax - b > k. Always check that the solutions satisfy any domain restrictions, especially when the right-hand side involves x.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to consider both positive and negative cases when removing absolute value, especially in inequalities. Also, failing to check that solutions satisfy the original equation when the right-hand side is an expression involving x.

concept_explanation: A function is a relation where each element in the domain maps to exactly one element in the codomain. The vertical line test checks if a graph represents a function: any vertical line should intersect the graph at most once. Domain is the set of all possible inputs, range is the set of outputs. The absolute value function f(x)=|ax+b| produces a V-shaped graph. Function notation f(x) expresses the rule. For example, question 3 shows a mapping from set A to set B with images {49,36}. This is a function if each input has one output.
worked_example: Question 3: Given set A = {7,6,-6,-7} and set B = {49,36}. The mapping shows 7→49, 6→36, -6→36, -7→49. Is it a function? Yes, because every element in set A maps to exactly one element in set B. Domain = {7,6,-6,-7}, Range = {49,36}. Using function notation, f(x)=x^2 or f(x)=|x|^2.
common_mistakes: Students often think a relation is not a function if the outputs are repeated. But a function allows many inputs to map to the same output, as long as each input has only one output.

concept_explanation: A composite function is formed when one function is substituted into another. If f and g are two functions, the composite function f[g(x)] is obtained by substituting g(x) into f(x). Similarly, g[f(x)] is obtained by substituting f(x) into g(x). For example, given f(r) = πr^2 and r = g(t) = 100t, the composite function A = f[g(t)] = π(100t)^2 = 10,000πt^2 represents the area of an oil spill as a function of time.
worked_example:
Given f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = x^2. Find f[g(x)] and g[f(x)].
Solution:
f[g(x)] = f(x^2) = x^2 + 2.
g[f(x)] = g(x + 2) = (x + 2)^2 = x^2 + 4x + 4.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse the order of composition, e.g., thinking f[g(x)] equals g[f(x)]. The functions are generally not commutative.

concept_explanation: The composition of two functions f and g, denoted as fg(x), is defined as f[g(x)], meaning that the output of g becomes the input of f. For functions f(x)=x+2 and g(x)=x², the composite function fg(x) is f[g(x)] = f(x²) = x²+2. The domain of fg is the set of x in the domain of g such that g(x) is in the domain of f. Composite functions are not commutative: fg(x) is generally not equal to gf(x).
worked_example:
Given f(x)=x+2 and g(x)=x². Determine fg(x) and gf(x). 
Solution: 
fg(x) = f[g(x)] = f(x²) = x²+2. 
gf(x) = g[f(x)] = g(x+2) = (x+2)² = x²+4x+4. 
Thus, fg(x) = x²+2 and gf(x) = x²+4x+4.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse the order of composition, writing fg(x) as g[f(x)] instead of f[g(x)] or incorrectly treating fg(x) as the product f(x)⋅g(x). Always remember that fg(x) means apply g first, then f.

concept_explanation: A composite function is formed when two functions are combined such that the output of one function becomes the input of another. If f and g are functions, the composite function fg (read as 'f composed with g') is defined as fg(x) = f[g(x)]. Similarly, gf(x) = g[f(x)]. Note that f² denotes ff, i.e., f composed with itself: f²(x) = f[f(x)]. Composite functions are not necessarily commutative; fg and gf may be different.
worked_example:
Example 8: Given f(x)=2x and g(x)=x²–5, find (a) fg, (b) gf, (c) f², (d) g².
(a) fg(x)=f[g(x)]=f(x²–5)=2(x²–5)=2x²–10. Thus fg : x→2x²–10.
(b) gf(x)=g[f(x)]=g(2x)=(2x)²–5=4x²–5. Thus gf : x→4x²–5.
(c) f²(x)=f[f(x)]=f(2x)=2(2x)=4x. Thus f² : x→4x.
(d) g²(x)=g[g(x)]=g(x²–5)=(x²–5)²–5=x⁴–10x²+25–5=x⁴–10x²+20. Thus g² : x→x⁴–10x²+20.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse the order of composition, e.g., writing fg as g[f(x)] instead of f[g(x)]. Also, when computing f², they may mistakenly square the function notation instead of applying the function twice.

subtopic: 1.2.3 Determining the image or object of a composite function
concept_explanation: A composite function combines two functions, such as fg(x) which means apply g first, then f. To find the image, substitute the object value into the composite function. If the image is given, equate the composite function to that value and solve the equation to find the object.
worked_example: Example: If f: x → x – 1 and g: x → x² – 3x + 4, find (a) fg(2) and gf(1), (b) the values of x when fg(x) = 7. Solution: (a) fg(x) = f[g(x)] = f(x² – 3x + 4) = x² – 3x + 4 – 1 = x² – 3x + 3. Thus fg(2) = 4 – 6 + 3 = 1. gf(x) = g[f(x)] = g(x – 1) = (x – 1)² – 3(x – 1) + 4 = x² – 2x + 1 – 3x + 3 + 4 = x² – 5x + 8. Thus gf(1) = 1 – 5 + 8 = 4. (b) fg(x) = 7 ⇒ x² – 3x + 3 = 7 ⇒ x² – 3x – 4 = 0 ⇒ (x + 1)(x – 4) = 0 ⇒ x = –1 or x = 4.
common_mistakes: Students often reverse the order of composition: fg(x) means g first, then f. They may also forget to substitute correctly when functions are given as mappings, leading to incorrect algebraic expressions.

subtopic: Determining a function when the composite function and one of the functions are given
concept_explanation: When the composite function and one of the functions are given, the other function can be determined using substitution or algebraic manipulation. For fg(x) given, substitute the known f into fg and solve for g(x). For gf(x) given, use substitution by letting y = f(x) to express g(y) in terms of y, then replace y with x.
common_mistakes: For gf given, students often incorrectly substitute directly instead of using the substitution method. Ensure to replace the variable correctly.

concept_explanation: A composite function combines two functions where the output of one function becomes the input of another. If function q maps n (number of workers) to q (quantity produced), and function r maps q to revenue, then the composite function r(q(n)) gives revenue directly as a function of workers. This models real-world scenarios where a quantity depends on another via a chain of relationships.
worked_example: Example: The total production per day, q, of a factory depends on the number of workers, n, by q(n) = 10n - ¼ n². The total revenue per day, r, from selling q goods is r(q) = 40q. Determine the total revenue when there are 20 workers. Solution: The composite function r(q(n)) = 40(10n - ¼ n²) = 400n - 10n². Substitute n = 20: r(20) = 400(20) - 10(20)² = 8000 - 4000 = 4000. Thus, the total revenue is RM4000.
common_mistakes: A common mistake is confusing the order of composition (e.g., computing q(r(n)) instead of r(q(n))). Another is incorrectly expanding or simplifying the composite expression, such as forgetting to apply the outer function to the entire output of the inner function.

concept_explanation: Composite functions combine two functions by applying one after the other. If f and g are functions, the composite function f∘g is defined as (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)). The domain of f∘g consists of all x in the domain of g such that g(x) lies in the domain of f. Iterated functions, such as f²(x) = f(f(x)), are repeated compositions of the same function. Composite functions are widely used to model real-world situations where one quantity depends on another through a chain of relationships.
worked_example:
A factory's daily revenue r (in RM) is a function of the number of workers n, given by r(n) = 400n – 10n². Find the number of workers that gives a daily revenue of RM4 000, and determine the revenue when there are 20 workers.

Solution:
Set r(n) = 4 000:
4 000 = 400n – 10n²
10n² – 400n + 4 000 = 0
n² – 40n + 400 = 0
(n – 20)(n – 20) = 0
n = 20
Thus, 20 workers give RM4 000 daily revenue.
Check: r(20) = 400(20) – 10(20)² = 8 000 – 4 000 = 4 000.
The daily revenue with 20 workers is RM4 000.
common_mistakes: Confusing the order of composition; assuming f∘g = g∘f. Also, forgetting to check that the output of the inner function lies in the domain of the outer function.

concept_explanation: A composite function is formed when two functions are combined such that the output of one function becomes the input of the other. The composite function fg (read as 'f after g') is defined as f(g(x)), and gf is g(f(x)). To find the composite function, substitute the expression of the inner function into the outer function.
common_mistakes: When finding composite functions, students sometimes apply the functions in the wrong order (e.g., treat fg as applying f first). Also, they may forget to exclude values that make the denominator zero in rational composite functions.

concept_explanation: Inverse functions reverse the input and output of a function. If f maps x to y, its inverse f⁻¹ maps y back to x, written as f(x)=y ⇔ f⁻¹(y)=x. The graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of the graph of f across the line y=x. For a function to have an inverse, it must be one-to-one.
worked_example: Given F(C) = (9/5)C + 32 converts Celsius to Fahrenheit, its inverse is C(F) = (5/9)(F-32). Substitute F=39: C = (5/9)(39-32) = (5/9)×7 ≈ 3.89°C.
common_mistakes: Assuming any function has an inverse without checking one-to-one property. Forgetting the domain restriction when finding inverse of a non-one-to-one function.

concept_title: Inverse Functions from Arrow Diagrams and Algebra
concept_explanation: The inverse function, denoted as f⁻¹, reverses the mapping of f. If f maps x to y, then f⁻¹ maps y back to x, i.e., f(x) = y ⇔ f⁻¹(y) = x. In an arrow diagram, to find f⁻¹(a), locate the output a and trace backward to its input. Algebraically, to find f⁻¹(k), set f(x) = k and solve for x, provided f is one-to-one. Note that f⁻¹ does not mean reciprocal; f⁻¹(x) ≠ 1/f(x).
worked_example:
Example: In an arrow diagram, f(2) = 1, f(4) = 1/2, f(3) = 5. (a) f⁻¹(4) = 2. (b) f⁻¹(5) = 3.

Example: Given f(x) = x/(x-4), x ≠ 4. (a) f(2) = 2/(2-4) = -1. (b) Find f⁻¹(3): Let a = f⁻¹(3), then f(a) = 3 → a/(a-4) = 3 → a = 3(a-4) → a = 3a - 12 → 2a = 12 → a = 6. Thus f⁻¹(3) = 6.
common_mistakes: Treating f⁻¹ as 1/f(x). For example, incorrectly writing f⁻¹(x) = 1/f(x). Also, forgetting domain restrictions when solving algebraically, such as noting that x ≠ 4 in f(x) = x/(x-4).

concept_explanation: A function has an inverse function if and only if it is a one-to-one function (injective). This means every element in the codomain is mapped from exactly one element in the domain. For a function f: X → Y, its inverse f⁻¹: Y → X exists only when f is one-to-one. The inverse function reverses the mapping, sending each element of the codomain back to its unique original element in the domain.
worked_example: Consider function h: C → D defined by h(x) = x + 2, where C = {-2, 0, 2, 4} and D = {0, 2, 4, 6}. Mapping: -2→0, 0→2, 2→4, 4→6. Since each input gives a distinct output, h is one-to-one. Its inverse h⁻¹: D → C is defined by h⁻¹(y) = y - 2, with mapping: 0→-2, 2→0, 4→2, 6→4, which is also a function. In contrast, function g: A → B with g(x) = x², A = {-1, 1}, B = {1} maps both -1 and 1 to 1, so g is not one-to-one. Its inverse would need to map 1 to both -1 and 1, which is not a function.
common_mistakes: Assuming every function has an inverse without checking the one-to-one condition. For example, confusing the inverse of a function with its reciprocal (e.g., mistaking f⁻¹(x) for 1/f(x)).

concept_explanation: Two functions f and g are inverses of each other if and only if the composite functions fg(x) = x for all x in the domain of g and gf(x) = x for all x in the domain of f. This means that applying f then g (or g then f) returns the original input. Additionally, the domain of f equals the range of g, and the domain of g equals the range of f. The graph of g is the reflection of the graph of f across the line y = x.
common_mistakes: Students may incorrectly think that fg(x) = x is sufficient for inverses without also checking gf(x) = x, or may confuse the domain and range when determining the inverse function.

concept_explanation: If two functions f and g are inverse functions of each other, then the domain of f equals the range of g, and the domain of g equals the range of f. Additionally, the graph of g is the reflection of the graph of f across the line y = x. For any point (a, b) on the graph of f, its reflection (b, a) lies on the graph of g. To determine if a function has an inverse, use the horizontal line test: if every horizontal line intersects the graph at most once, the function is one-to-one and has an inverse; otherwise, it does not.
common_mistakes: A common mistake is assuming that every function has an inverse, but only one-to-one functions satisfy the horizontal line test and possess an inverse.

concept_explanation: A function f has an inverse function if and only if it is a one-to-one function, meaning each element in the codomain is mapped from at most one element in the domain. The horizontal line test can be used to check this: if any horizontal line intersects the graph of f at more than one point, then f is not one-to-one and has no inverse. Alternatively, we can verify by showing that f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x for functions f and g, implying they are inverses.
worked_example:
Example 15: Determine whether each function f has an inverse.
(a) f is one-to-one as every element in domain maps to unique element in codomain. Thus, inverse exists.
(b) Horizontal line test: any horizontal line cuts graph at one point → one-to-one → inverse exists.
(c) Horizontal line test: line cuts graph at two points → not one-to-one → no inverse.

Example 16: Verify f(x)=3−2x and g(x)=(3−x)/2 are inverses.
Solution: fg(x)=f(g(x))=3−2[(3−x)/2]=3−(3−x)=x.
gf(x)=g(f(x))=(3−(3−2x))/2=(2x)/2=x.
Since fg(x)=x and gf(x)=x, f and g are inverse functions.
common_mistakes: Assuming every function has an inverse. Many functions (e.g., f(x)=x²) are not one-to-one unless domain is restricted.

concept_explanation: Graf bagi fungsi songsang f⁻¹ ialah pantulan graf f pada garis lurus y = x. Domain bagi f⁻¹ adalah sama dengan julat bagi f. Untuk melakar graf f⁻¹, kita boleh memplot titik-titik pada graf f, kemudian pantulkannya pada garis y = x, atau menggunakan jadual nilai dengan menukar koordinat (x, y) kepada (y, x).
worked_example:
Contoh 17: Fungsi f ditakrifkan oleh f : x → x² – 6 untuk domain 0 < x < 4. Lakarkan graf f dan f⁻¹ pada satah yang sama. Seterusnya, nyatakan domain bagi f⁻¹.
Penyelesaian: Graf f ialah sebahagian daripada lengkung kuadratik y = x² – 6. Dengan memplot titik-titik dalam jadual nilai (x: 0,1,2,3,4; y: -6,-5,-2,3,10), graf f dilakar. Graf f⁻¹ ialah pantulan graf f pada garis y = x. Domain f⁻¹ ialah julat f, iaitu –6 ≤ x ≤ 10.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa ialah tertukar antara domain dan julat apabila menentukan domain fungsi songsang. Ingat bahawa domain f⁻¹ = julat f dan julat f⁻¹ = domain f.

concept_explanation: An inverse function reverses the effect of the original function. For two functions f and g to be inverses of each other, they must satisfy f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) = x for all x in the domains. To find the inverse function algebraically, replace f(x) with y, swap x and y, then solve for y. The resulting expression is f⁻¹(x). The graph of an inverse function is the reflection of the original function across the line y = x.
worked_example: Example: Given f(x) = 3x - 2, find f⁻¹(x). Solution: Let y = 3x - 2. Swap x and y: x = 3y - 2. Solve for y: 3y = x + 2, so y = (x + 2)/3. Thus, f⁻¹(x) = (x + 2)/3. Verify: f(f⁻¹(x)) = 3[(x+2)/3] - 2 = x + 2 - 2 = x, and f⁻¹(f(x)) = [(3x-2)+2]/3 = 3x/3 = x. Hence, they are inverses.
common_mistakes: Students often forget to swap x and y before solving, or incorrectly solve for y. They may also assume that f(g(x)) = x alone is sufficient without checking both compositions.

concept_explanation: An inverse function f⁻¹ maps each element in the range of f back to its original domain. To find f⁻¹(x), replace f(x) with y, solve for x in terms of y, then swap y with x. The inverse exists only if f is a one-to-one function. Verification can be done using the property ff⁻¹(x) = f⁻¹f(x) = x.
worked_example:
Given f: x → 5x + 2, find (a) f⁻¹(x), (b) f⁻¹(7).
Solution: (a) Let y = 5x + 2, then 5x = y - 2, x = (y - 2)/5. Replace y with x, so f⁻¹(x) = (x - 2)/5. (b) f⁻¹(7) = (7 - 2)/5 = 1.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to swap variables at the final step or not verifying that the original function is one-to-one before finding its inverse.

concept_explanation: Composite functions combine two functions, where the output of one becomes the input of another, denoted as gf(x) = g(f(x)). Inverse functions reverse the mapping of a one-to-one function, denoted as f⁻¹(y) = x if f(x) = y. The horizontal line test determines if a function is one-to-one and thus has an inverse. For composite functions, the inverse is the composition of the inverses in reverse order: (gf)⁻¹ = f⁻¹g⁻¹.
worked_example: Given an arrow diagram where f maps 2 to 5 and 5 to 8, and g maps 5 to 8 and 8 to z: (a) f(2)=5, (b) g(5)=8, (c) gf(2)=g(f(2))=g(5)=8, (d) f⁻¹(5)=2, (e) g⁻¹(8)=5, (f) f⁻¹g⁻¹(8)=f⁻¹(g⁻¹(8))=f⁻¹(5)=2.
common_mistakes: Students often misinterpret f⁻¹(x) as 1/f(x) instead of the inverse function. Also, when finding the inverse of a composite function, the order of composition is reversed.

concept_explanation: Fungsi songsang, ditulis sebagai f⁻¹, memetakan imej kembali kepada objek asal. Hanya fungsi satu-ke-satu mempunyai fungsi songsang. Sifat penting: jika g(x) = f⁻¹(x), maka f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) = x. Graf f⁻¹ adalah pantulan graf f pada garis y = x. Dalam konteks isipadu sfera V = (4/3)πr³, fungsi songsang memberikan r = ∛(3V/(4π)).
worked_example: Zaki ingin membuat bola air sfera yang boleh menampung 1 cm³ air. Diberi V = (4/3)πr³. (a) Fungsi f: r → V, f(r) = (4/3)πr³. Fungsi songsang f⁻¹: V → r, f⁻¹(V) = ∛(3V/(4π)). (b) Apabila V = 1 cm³, r = ∛(3×1/(4π)) = ∛(3/(4π)) ≈ 0.620 cm (kepada 3 angka bererti).
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering lupa bahawa hanya fungsi satu-ke-satu mempunyai songsang. Mereka juga mungkin tersilap menyelesaikan persamaan bagi r, seperti tidak menggunakan punca kuasa tiga dengan betul.

concept_explanation: A composite function, denoted as fg(x) or f(g(x)), is formed when the output of one function becomes the input of another. For a function to have an inverse, it must be one-to-one; its inverse f⁻¹ maps each output back to its unique input. The inverse can be found by swapping x and y in the equation y = f(x) and solving for y. For example, if f(x) = 2x + 3, then f⁻¹(x) = (x - 3)/2.
worked_example:
Given f(x) = 3x - 2 and fg(x) = 6x + 1, find g(x).
Solution: f(g(x)) = 3g(x) - 2 = 6x + 1
3g(x) = 6x + 3
g(x) = 2x + 1.
common_mistakes: Assuming all functions have inverses without checking if they are one-to-one. For non-one-to-one functions, the domain must be restricted before finding an inverse.

concept_explanation: Composite functions allow us to combine two related functions. For example, if cost C is given as a function of quantity x, and price p is also a function of x, we can express C as a function of p by solving for x in terms of p and substituting into C(x). This is useful in economics to relate cost to selling price.
worked_example:
Given demand equation p = 100 - (1/4)x for 0 < x < 400, and cost C = x/25 + 600. (a) Express C as a function of p. (b) Find C when p = RM36.
Solution:
(a) From p = 100 - x/4, we get x = 400 - 4p. Substitute into C: C(p) = (400 - 4p)/25 + 600 = 16 - (4/25)p + 600 = 616 - (4/25)p.
(b) When p = 36, C = 616 - (4/25)*36 = 616 - 5.76 = RM610.24.
common_mistakes: Students may forget to solve for x correctly or omit the domain condition (0 < x < 400). Also, ensure the final function is correctly simplified.

concept_explanation: A quadratic equation is an equation with a variable of degree 2. The general form is ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, and c are constants and a ≠ 0. Solving a quadratic equation means finding the values of the variable that satisfy the equation, which are called the roots or solutions. For instance, the equation x² + 3x - 100 = 0 is a quadratic equation derived from a geometry problem involving a rectangular picture frame.
worked_example: Given a rectangular picture frame with area 100 cm². Width = x cm, length = (x+3) cm. Then area = x(x+3) = 100 → x² + 3x - 100 = 0. This is a quadratic equation in general form.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the coefficient a cannot be zero; otherwise the equation becomes linear, not quadratic.

concept_title: Completing the Square for Quadratic Equations
concept_explanation: Completing the square is a method to solve quadratic equations by rewriting them in the form (x + p)^2 = q. First, ensure the coefficient of x^2 is 1. Then move the constant term to the right side, add (coefficient of x / 2)^2 to both sides, and factor the left side as a perfect square. Taking square roots gives the solutions. For example, x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0 becomes (x + 2)^2 = 11, leading to x = -2 ± √11.
worked_example:
Example 1: Solve x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0 by completing the square.
Step 1: x^2 + 4x = 7
Step 2: Add (4/2)^2 = 4 to both sides: x^2 + 4x + 4 = 7 + 4 → (x + 2)^2 = 11
Step 3: x + 2 = ±√11 → x = -5.317 or x = 1.317.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide all terms by the coefficient of x^2 if it is not 1 before completing the square, e.g., for -3x^2 + 6x - 1 = 0, one must first divide by -3.

concept_explanation: The quadratic formula provides a direct method to solve any quadratic equation of the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are constants and a ≠ 0. It is given by x = [-b ± sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a). The term b^2 - 4ac is called the discriminant, which determines the nature of the roots. This formula is derived by completing the square and works for all quadratic equations, even when factorization is complex or impossible.
worked_example:
Solve the equation 2x^2 – 2x – 3 = 0 by using the formula.

Solution: Compare with ax^2 + bx + c = 0 → a = 2, b = –2, c = –3.
Substitute into the formula:
x = [–(–2) ± sqrt((–2)^2 – 4(2)(–3))] / (2(2))
= [2 ± sqrt(4 + 24)] / 4
= [2 ± sqrt(28)] / 4
Simplify: x = (2 + sqrt28)/4 ≈ 1.823  or  x = (2 – sqrt28)/4 ≈ –0.823.
Hence, the solutions are –0.823 and 1.823.
common_mistakes: A common error is incorrectly substituting the signs of b and c, especially when b is negative. For example, some students write –(–2) as –2 instead of 2. Another mistake is forgetting the ± symbol, which leads to missing one solution. Also, errors in simplifying the square root or arithmetic in the denominator can occur.

subtopic: Forming Quadratic Equations from Given Roots
concept_explanation: Given two roots α and β, the quadratic equation can be formed using the sum and product of roots. The standard form is x² - (α+β)x + αβ = 0, derived from the factorised form (x - α)(x - β) = 0. In the general quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is α+β = -b/a and the product is αβ = c/a.
worked_example: Example: Form a quadratic equation with roots 2 and 3. Solution: Sum = 2+3=5, Product = 2×3=6. Equation: x² - 5x + 6 = 0.
common_mistakes: Common mistake: Writing the equation as x² + (α+β)x + αβ = 0, forgetting the negative sign for the sum term.

concept_title: Forming Quadratic Equations from Given Roots
concept_explanation: Given two roots α and β of a quadratic equation, a new quadratic equation can be formed using the sum and product of the roots. For new roots, calculate their sum (S) and product (P), then the required equation is x² – Sx + P = 0. If necessary, clear fractions by multiplying both sides by the common denominator to obtain integer coefficients.
worked_example:
Example 4: If α and β are the roots of 2x² + x = 4, form equations with roots (a) α+3, β+3; (b) 2α, 2β; (c) α², β².
Solution:
First rewrite as 2x² + x – 4 = 0. Here a=2, b=1, c=–4. Then α+β = –b/a = –½, αβ = c/a = –2.
(a) Sum = (α+3)+(β+3) = (α+β)+6 = –½ + 6 = 11/2. Product = (α+3)(β+3) = αβ + 3(α+β) + 9 = –2 + 3(–½) + 9 = –2 – 3/2 + 9 = 11/2. Equation: x² – (11/2)x + 11/2 = 0 → multiply by 2: 2x² – 11x + 11 = 0.
(b) Sum = 2α+2β = 2(α+β) = 2(–½) = –1. Product = (2α)(2β) = 4αβ = 4(–2) = –8. Equation: x² – (–1)x + (–8) = 0 → x² + x – 8 = 0.
(c) Sum = α²+β² = (α+β)² – 2αβ = (–½)² – 2(–2) = ¼ + 4 = 17/4. Product = α²β² = (αβ)² = (–2)² = 4. Equation: x² – (17/4)x + 4 = 0 → multiply by 4: 4x² – 17x + 16 = 0.
common_mistakes: A common mistake is forgetting to multiply the entire equation when clearing fractions after obtaining fractional sum or product, leading to an invalid equation. Another error is incorrectly calculating α²+β² using (α+β)² – 2αβ, which is correct, but sometimes students mistakenly write (α+β)² – αβ.

concept_explanation: Ketaksamaan kuadratik dalam satu pemboleh ubah ialah ketaksamaan yang melibatkan ungkapan kuadratik. Untuk menyelesaikannya, cari julat nilai x yang memenuhi ketaksamaan tersebut. Tiga kaedah yang boleh digunakan ialah lakaran graf, garis nombor, dan jadual. Contohnya, untuk (x+1)(x-3) > 0, punca-punca ialah -1 dan 3, dan penyelesaiannya ialah x < -1 atau x > 3.
worked_example: Selesaikan (x+1)(x-3) < 0 menggunakan kaedah lakaran graf. Lakarkan graf y = (x+1)(x-3). Graf adalah parabola yang terbuka ke atas dengan punca pada x = -1 dan x = 3. Carikan bahagian graf di bawah paksi-x (y < 0). Bahagian itu adalah antara x = -1 dan x = 3. Maka penyelesaiannya ialah -1 < x < 3.
common_mistakes: Punca ketaksamaan tidak dianggap dengan betul apabila menanda garis nombor, atau terlupa menukar arah ketaksamaan apabila mendarab dengan nombor negatif dalam kaedah jadual.

concept_title: Solving Quadratic Inequalities by Number Line and Table
concept_explanation: A quadratic inequality such as (x+1)(x-3)>0 can be solved using number line and table methods. The number line method involves marking the roots (e.g., -1 and 3) and testing sample points in each interval to determine the sign of the expression. Similarly, the table method organizes the signs of each factor and their product for intervals defined by the roots. The conclusion states that for (x-a)(x-b)=0 with a<b: if (x-a)(x-b)>0, then x<a or x>b; if (x-a)(x-b)<0, then a<x<b.
common_mistakes: Common mistake: incorrectly labeling test points or forgetting that a<x<b means x is strictly between the roots, not including the endpoints.

concept_explanation: Quadratic inequalities are solved by first rewriting them in standard form ax² + bx + c ≥ 0 or ≤ 0. The roots of the corresponding quadratic equation are found, dividing the number line into intervals. Three methods can determine the solution interval: graph sketching (parabola above/below x-axis), number line testing (positive/negative signs across intervals), or a table of signs. The solution is the set of x-values satisfying the inequality.
worked_example:
Example 5: Find the range of values of x for (2x – 1)(x + 4) ≥ x + 4 using (a) graph sketching, (b) number line, (c) table method.

Solution:
Simplify: (2x – 1)(x + 4) ≥ x + 4 → 2x² + 7x – 4 ≥ x + 4 → 2x² + 6x – 8 ≥ 0 → x² + 3x – 4 ≥ 0 → (x + 4)(x – 1) ≥ 0.
Roots: x = –4 or x = 1.

(a) Graph sketching method: Sketch y = (x + 4)(x – 1). The parabola opens upward, crosses x-axis at –4 and 1. For (x + 4)(x – 1) ≥ 0, the graph lies above or on the x-axis. Hence, x ≤ –4 or x ≥ 1.

(b) Number line method: Test intervals (-∞, –4), (–4, 1), (1, ∞) using test points x = –5, 0, 2. For (x+4)(x-1): at x = –5 → (+)(–) = –; at x = 0 → (+)(–) = –; at x = 2 → (+)(+) = +. Since product ≥ 0, we take positive regions: x ≤ –4 or x ≥ 1.

(c) Table method: Construct a table with intervals x ≤ –4, –4 ≤ x ≤ 1, x ≥ 1. Signs: (x+4) → –, +, +; (x–1) → –, –, +; product → +, –, +. Since product ≥ 0, choose positive regions: x ≤ –4 or x ≥ 1.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to bring all terms to one side before factoring, incorrectly identifying the inequality direction when multiplying/dividing by a negative number, or misinterpreting the sign of the quadratic coefficient when graph sketching.

concept_explanation: A quadratic inequality is an inequality involving a quadratic expression, such as ax^2 + bx + c < 0, > 0, ≤ 0, or ≥ 0. To solve it, rewrite the inequality so one side is zero, then factorise or find the roots. Use one of three methods: graph sketching (draw the parabola and read the solution interval), number line (test intervals between roots), or table method (tabulate sign of factors). For example, solve x^2 < 4 by rewriting as x^2 - 4 < 0, factor (x-2)(x+2) < 0, and the solution is -2 < x < 2.
worked_example:
Solve (2 – x)(8 – x) < 0.
Step 1: Expand: (2-x)(8-x) = 16 - 2x - 8x + x^2 = x^2 - 10x + 16 < 0. Roots are x = 2 and x = 8.
Step 2: Draw number line with roots 2 and 8. Test x = 0: (2-0)(8-0)=16>0. Test x=5: (2-5)(8-5)= -3 <0. Test x=9: (2-9)(8-9)=7>0.
Step 3: The inequality is <0, so the solution is 2 < x < 8.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to consider the direction of the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative number. Also, incorrectly including the endpoints when the inequality is strict (< or >).

concept_explanation: Jenis punca persamaan kuadratik ax² + bx + c = 0 ditentukan oleh nilai diskriminan, D = b² – 4ac. Jika D > 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata yang berbeza. Jika D = 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata yang sama (punca ulangan). Jika D < 0, persamaan tidak mempunyai punca nyata (punca adalah nombor kompleks). Diskriminan digunakan untuk mengenal pasti bilangan dan jenis punca tanpa perlu menyelesaikan persamaan.
worked_example: Persamaan 9x² – 6x + 2 = 0: a=9, b=-6, c=2. D = (-6)² – 4(9)(2) = 36 – 72 = -36 < 0. Maka persamaan ini tidak mempunyai punca nyata kerana diskriminan negatif.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering tersalah anggap bahawa D = 0 bermakna tiada punca, sedangkan ia memberikan dua punca yang sama. Juga, lupa bahawa D < 0 memberi punca khayalan (bukan 'tiada punca langsung').

concept_explanation: Diskriminan, D = b² - 4ac, menentukan jenis punca persamaan kuadratik ax² + bx + c = 0. Jika D > 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata dan berbeza. Jika D = 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata yang sama (punca berganda). Jika D < 0, persamaan tidak mempunyai punca nyata. Nilai diskriminan mesti dihitung terlebih dahulu untuk menentukan jenis punca.
worked_example:
Contoh 6: Tentukan jenis punca bagi setiap persamaan kuadratik berikut.
(a) x² + 5x - 6 = 0
a=1, b=5, c=-6, D = 5² - 4(1)(-6) = 25+24 = 49 > 0 → dua punca nyata dan berbeza.
(b) -4x² + 4x - 1 = 0
a=-4, b=4, c=-1, D = 4² - 4(-4)(-1) = 16 - 16 = 0 → dua punca nyata yang sama.
(c) 2x² - 4x + 5 = 0
a=2, b=-4, c=5, D = (-4)² - 4(2)(5) = 16 - 40 = -24 < 0 → tiada punca nyata.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa adalah tidak menulis persamaan dalam bentuk am ax²+bx+c=0 sebelum mengenal pasti a, b, c; atau tersilap menggunakan tanda negatif semasa mengira diskriminan.

concept_explanation: Diskriminan, D = b² – 4ac, menentukan sifat punca persamaan kuadratik ax² + bx + c = 0. Jika D > 0, terdapat dua punca nyata dan berbeza; jika D = 0, dua punca nyata dan sama; jika D < 0, tiada punca nyata. Nilai diskriminan digunakan untuk mencari keadaan parameter dalam persamaan kuadratik.
worked_example: Cari nilai k supaya persamaan x² + k + 3 = kx mempunyai dua punca sama. Penyelesaian: Susun semula: x² – kx + k + 3 = 0, a = 1, b = –k, c = k + 3. D = (–k)² – 4(1)(k + 3) = k² – 4k – 12 = 0. Faktorkan: (k + 2)(k – 6) = 0, maka k = –2 atau k = 6.
common_mistakes: Ralat biasa: Tidak menyusun persamaan ke dalam bentuk am ax² + bx + c = 0 sebelum menggunakan diskriminan, menyebabkan nilai a, b, c salah.

Nilai diskriminan menentukan jenis punca: jika Δ > 0, dua punca nyata dan berbeza; jika Δ = 0, dua punca nyata dan sama; jika Δ < 0, tiada punca nyata. Untuk mencari julat parameter, pastikan persamaan ditulis dalam bentuk am terlebih dahulu.

concept_title: Effects of a, b, c on Graph of Quadratic Function
concept_explanation: A quadratic function in general form is f(x) = ax² + bx + c, where a, b, and c are constants and a ≠ 0. Its graph is a parabola symmetric about the axis of symmetry passing through the vertex (maximum or minimum point). The value of a determines whether the parabola opens upward (a > 0) or downward (a < 0). Changing b shifts the graph horizontally, and changing c shifts it vertically.
common_mistakes: Students often confuse the effect of b: changing b does not simply shift the graph left or right in a straightforward way; it also changes the position of the axis of symmetry.

subtopic: Kesan Perubahan Nilai a, b dan c terhadap Graf Fungsi Kuadratik
concept_title: Kesan Perubahan a, b, c pada Graf
concept_explanation: Bagi fungsi kuadratik f(x) = ax² + bx + c, perubahan nilai a mempengaruhi bentuk dan lebar graf tetapi pintasan-y kekal. Apabila a > 0, graf berbentuk ∪ (melalui titik minimum); apabila a < 0, graf berbentuk ∩ (melalui titik maksimum). Semakin besar |a|, semakin sempit graf; semakin kecil |a| (menghampiri 0), semakin lebar graf. Perubahan nilai b hanya mengubah kedudukan puncak (vertex) secara melintang; jika b = 0, puncak pada paksi-y. Bagi a > 0, b > 0 menggerakkan puncak ke kiri paksi-y dan b < 0 ke kanan; bagi a < 0, sebaliknya. Perubahan nilai c menggerakkan graf secara menegak ke atas (jika c bertambah) atau ke bawah (jika c berkurang) tanpa mengubah bentuk graf.
worked_example:
Contoh 9: Rajah menunjukkan lakaran graf f(x) = x² + 1 (a=1,b=0,c=1). Buat analisis dan generalisasi tentang bentuk dan kedudukan graf apabila nilai berikut berubah. Seterusnya, lakar graf. (a) Nilai a menjadi (i) 2, (ii) ½. (b) Nilai c menjadi 3.
Penyelesaian:
(a)(i) Apabila a berubah daripada 1 kepada 2, graf menjadi lebih sempit dan bentuk tetap ∪ (minimum). Pintasan-y masih 1.
(a)(ii) Apabila a berubah daripada 1 kepada ½, graf menjadi lebih lebar, bentuk tetap ∪ (minimum), pintasan-y masih 1.
(b) Apabila c berubah daripada 1 kepada 3, graf beralih ke atas sebanyak 2 unit, bentuk dan lebar tidak berubah, pintasan-y menjadi 3.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering tersalah anggap bahawa perubahan nilai b menggeser graf secara melintang seperti perubahan c secara menegak. Sebenarnya, b hanya mengubah kedudukan puncak secara melintang (kiri/kanan paksi-y) bergantung pada tanda a, bukan menggeser seluruh graf secara seragam.

subtopic: Relating the position of the graph of a quadratic function and the types of roots
concept_explanation: The discriminant, Δ = b² – 4ac, of a quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c determines the nature of its roots and the number of x-intercepts. If Δ > 0, the graph intersects the x-axis at two distinct points (two real and distinct roots). If Δ = 0, the graph touches the x-axis at one point (repeated real root). If Δ < 0, the graph does not intersect the x-axis (no real roots). The coefficient a determines whether the graph opens upward (a > 0) or downward (a < 0), but does not affect the root type.
common_mistakes: Students often think that a positive discriminant guarantees the graph opens upward, but discriminant only relates to the x-intercepts; the direction is determined solely by 'a'. Another mistake is confusing 'no real roots' with 'the graph lies entirely above the x-axis' – this is only true when a > 0; if a < 0, the graph lies entirely below the x-axis.

subtopic: 2.3.2 Hubungan antara Diskriminan dan Kedudukan Graf
concept_title: Discriminant and Graph Position of Quadratic Functions
concept_explanation: The discriminant, b² – 4ac, of a quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c determines the nature of its roots when f(x) = 0 and the position of its graph on the x-axis. For a positive leading coefficient (a > 0), the parabola opens upward; if b² – 4ac > 0, the graph intersects the x-axis at two distinct points; if = 0, it touches at one point (a repeated root); if < 0, it does not intersect. For a negative leading coefficient (a < 0), the parabola opens downward, with the same discriminant conditions applying to the number of x-intercepts.
worked_example: Example 10: Determine the types of roots for each quadratic function when f(x) = 0. Then sketch the graph. (a) f(x) = 2x² + x – 5: a=2, b=1, c=–5; discriminant = (1)² – 4(2)(–5) = 41 (> 0). Since a>0, the graph is a parabola opening upward, with two real and different roots, intersecting the x-axis at two points. (b) f(x) = –x² + 2x – 1: a=–1, b=2, c=–1; discriminant = (2)² – 4(–1)(–1) = 0. Since a<0, the graph is a parabola opening downward, with two real and equal roots, touching the x-axis at one point.
common_mistakes: Students often forget to consider the sign of 'a' when interpreting the graph position; a positive discriminant always gives two x-intercepts regardless of 'a', but the shape (opening up or down) depends on 'a'. Another common error is thinking discriminant = 0 means only one root, but mathematically there are two equal real roots.

concept_title: Menggunakan Diskriminan untuk Menentukan Sifat Graf
concept_explanation: Diskriminan, D = b² – 4ac, menentukan bilangan punca nyata bagi persamaan kuadratik dan seterusnya bilangan pintasan-x pada graf fungsi kuadratik. Jika D > 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata yang berbeza dan graf mempunyai dua pintasan-x. Jika D = 0, persamaan mempunyai dua punca nyata yang sama (punca ulangan) dan graf adalah tangen kepada paksi-x. Jika D < 0, persamaan tidak mempunyai punca nyata dan graf tiada pintasan-x.
worked_example:
Contoh 11:
(a) Cari nilai m supaya paksi-x adalah tangen kepada graf fungsi kuadratik f(x) = (m+1)x² + 4(m–2)x + 2m.
Penyelesaian: Tangen bermaksud dua punca nyata sama, maka b² – 4ac = 0. Gantikan a = m+1, b = 4(m–2), c = 2m:
(4(m–2))² – 4(m+1)(2m) = 0
16m² – 64m + 64 – 8m² – 8m = 0
8m² – 72m + 64 = 0
m² – 9m + 8 = 0
(m–1)(m–8)=0
m=1 atau m=8

(b) Cari julat nilai k jika graf fungsi kuadratik f(x) = 2x² + 5x + 3 – k tiada pintasan-x.
Penyelesaian: Tiada punca nyata, maka b² – 4ac < 0.
5² – 4(2)(3–k) < 0
25 – 24 + 8k < 0
1 + 8k < 0
k < –1/8

(c) Cari julat nilai p jika graf fungsi kuadratik f(x) = x² + px + p + 3 mempunyai dua pintasan-x.
Penyelesaian: Dua punca nyata berbeza, maka b² – 4ac > 0.
p² – 4(1)(p+3) > 0
p² – 4p – 12 > 0
(p+2)(p–6) > 0
p < –2 atau p > 6
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa ialah salah menentukan tanda ketaksamaan apabila menggunakan diskriminan. Ingat: tangen guna =0, tiada pintasan-x guna <0, dua pintasan-x guna >0. Juga, jangan lupa darab dengan betul semasa mengembangkan ungkapan.

subtopic: Perhubungan antara bentuk verteks dengan bentuk-bentuk lain fungsi kuadratik
concept_explanation: Bentuk verteks bagi fungsi kuadratik ialah f(x) = a(x – h)^2 + k, dengan a, h dan k ialah pemalar. Titik verteks ialah (h, k) dan graf adalah simetri pada garis x = h. Apabila a > 0, verteks ialah titik minimum dan k ialah nilai minimum; apabila a < 0, verteks ialah titik maksimum dan k ialah nilai maksimum. Bentuk ini boleh dihubungkan dengan bentuk am (ax^2 + bx + c) dan bentuk pintasan (a(x – p)(x – q)).
worked_example: Diberi f(x) = (x – 2)^2 – 9. Oleh kerana a = 1 > 0, graf berbentuk U. Verteks pada (2, –9) merupakan titik minimum. Paksi simetri ialah x = 2. Nilai minimum f(x) ialah –9.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa adalah menyangka verteks bagi f(x) = a(x – h)^2 + k ialah (–h, k) kerana terlupa tanda tolak dalam kurungan. Ingat bahawa (x – h) bermaksud koordinat-x bagi verteks ialah h.

subtopic: 2.3.3 Relation between Vertex Form, General Form, and Intercept Form
concept_explanation: A quadratic function can be expressed in three equivalent forms: vertex form f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k, general form f(x)=ax^2+bx+c, and intercept form f(x)=a(x-p)(x-q). These forms can be converted using expansion, factorisation, or completing the square. The graph of the quadratic function is the same regardless of the form used.
worked_example: Given f(x) = (x-4)^2-4. Expand to general form: f(x)=x^2-8x+12. Factorise to intercept form: f(x)=(x-2)(x-6).
common_mistakes: Students often make sign errors when expanding or completing the square, and may think that the different forms represent different functions instead of the same function.

concept_title: Menukar Bentuk Verteks ke Bentuk Pencegahan
concept_explanation: Tidak semua fungsi kuadratik boleh ditulis dalam bentuk pencegahan f(x) = a(x – p)(x – q), di mana a, p dan q adalah pemalar dan p, q ialah pintasan-x. Hanya graf yang mempunyai pintasan-x (iaitu punca nyata) boleh diungkapkan dalam bentuk ini. Untuk menukar, kita perlu menukarkan bentuk verteks ke bentuk am terlebih dahulu, kemudian faktorkan untuk mendapatkan bentuk pencegahan.
worked_example:
Tukarkan fungsi kuadratik f(x) = 2(x + 4)² – ¹⁄₈? (berdasarkan contoh asal) sebenarnya:

Diberi f(x) = 2(x + 4)² – (81/8)? (OCR tidak tepat, tetapi jawapan akhir adalah seperti di bawah)

Penyelesaian:
1. Kembangkan ke bentuk am: f(x) = 2x² + 9x + 10.
2. Faktorkan: 2x² + 9x + 10 = (2x + 5)(x + 2).
3. Tulis dalam bentuk pencegahan: f(x) = 2(x + ⁵⁄₂)(x + 2).
Maka, a = 2, p = –⁵⁄₂, q = –2.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering lupa bahawa bentuk pencegahan hanya boleh digunakan jika fungsi kuadratik mempunyai pintasan-x. Jika tiada punca nyata (diskriminan < 0), maka bentuk pencegahan tidak wujud.

subtopic: Analysing the effect of change of a, h and k on the shape and position of graph for f(x) = a(x – h)² + k
concept_title: Effect of a, h, k on Quadratic Graph
concept_explanation: In the vertex form f(x) = a(x - h)² + k, the vertex is at (h, k) and the axis of symmetry is x = h. The parameter 'a' determines the direction and width of the parabola: if a > 0, it opens upward (minimum point); if a < 0, it opens downward (maximum point). The magnitude of a affects the steepness. 'h' translates the graph horizontally, and 'k' translates it vertically. Changing h shifts the axis of symmetry and vertex left or right; changing k shifts the vertex up or down.
worked_example: Example: Convert f(x) = 2(x – 3)² – 8 into intercept form. Solution: Expand: f(x) = 2(x² – 6x + 9) – 8 = 2x² – 12x + 18 – 8 = 2x² – 12x + 10. Factor: = 2(x² – 6x + 5) = 2(x – 1)(x – 5). So intercept form: f(x) = 2(x – 1)(x – 5).
common_mistakes: Students often mistakenly think the vertex is at (-h, k) when using f(x) = a(x + h)² + k. Remember: for f(x) = a(x – h)² + k, the vertex is (h, k). Also, a negative 'a' gives a maximum, not a minimum.

subtopic: Kesan Perubahan Nilai a, h dan k terhadap Graf Fungsi Kuadratik
concept_title: Perubahan Bentuk dan Kedudukan Graf f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k
concept_explanation: Bagi fungsi kuadratik dalam bentuk f(x)=a(x-h)^2+k, perubahan nilai a mempengaruhi bentuk dan lebar graf. Jika a>0, graf berbentuk U dan melalui titik minimum; jika a<0, graf berbentuk ∩ dan melalui titik maksimum. Semakin besar nilai |a|, semakin sempit graf. Perubahan nilai h menyebabkan graf bergerak secara melintang: h meningkat, graf ke kanan; h menurun, graf ke kiri. Perubahan nilai k menyebabkan graf bergerak secara menegak: k meningkat, graf ke atas; k menurun, graf ke bawah. Paksi simetri hanya dipengaruhi oleh h, manakala nilai maksimum atau minimum hanya dipengaruhi oleh k.
worked_example: Contoh 14: Diberi graf f(x)=2(x+2)^2+3 dengan a=2, h=-2, k=3. Buat generalisasi tentang kesan perubahan setiap nilai berikut terhadap bentuk dan kedudukan graf: (a) nilai a berubah kepada 6 dan 1/3, (b) nilai h berubah kepada -6, (c) nilai k berubah kepada 8. Penyelesaian: (a) Apabila a=6 (lebih besar), graf menjadi lebih sempit; apabila a=1/3 (lebih kecil), graf menjadi lebih lebar. (b) Apabila h=-6 (lebih kecil), graf beralih ke kiri sebanyak 4 unit. (c) Apabila k=8 (lebih besar), graf beralih ke atas sebanyak 5 unit.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa: Pelajar tersalah arah pergerakan graf apabila nilai h berubah (contoh: menyangka h positif menggerakkan graf ke kiri) atau menganggap perubahan a mengubah kedudukan paksi simetri.

subtopic: Effects of Changing a, h and k on the Graph of f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k
concept_explanation: The quadratic function in vertex form is f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k, where (h, k) is the vertex. The value of a determines the width and direction: |a| > 1 makes the graph narrower, 0 < |a| < 1 makes it wider, and a < 0 reflects it downwards. Changing h shifts the graph horizontally (right if h increases, left if h decreases), while changing k shifts it vertically (up if k increases, down if k decreases). The axis of symmetry is x = h, and the vertex moves with h and k.
common_mistakes: Students often think that f(x) = (x - 4)^2 shifts the graph 4 units left instead of right. Remember: (x - h) shifts right for positive h, left for negative h.

subtopic: Mentafsir dan Melakar Graf Fungsi Kuadratik
concept_explanation: Untuk melakar graf fungsi kuadratik f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, ikuti langkah berikut: (1) Tentukan nilai a: jika a > 0, graf berbentuk U (titik minimum); jika a < 0, graf berbentuk ∩ (titik maksimum). (2) Hitung nilai diskriminan, b^2 – 4ac, untuk mengetahui bilangan titik persilangan dengan paksi-x: jika > 0, dua titik; jika = 0, satu titik (paksi-x tangen); jika < 0, tiada persilangan. (3) Cari punca-punca dengan menyelesaikan f(x) = 0 (persilangan paksi-x). (4) Cari pintasan-y dengan gantikan x = 0. (5) Tentukan titik verteks (pusingan) menggunakan kaedah penyempurnaan kuasa dua atau formula x = -b/(2a) dan y = f(-b/(2a)). Verteks juga merupakan titik maksimum atau minimum. (6) Plot titik-titik yang diperoleh dan lukis parabola yang simetri pada garis x = -b/(2a).
worked_example:
Contoh 15: Lakarkan graf fungsi kuadratik f(x) = –x² + 4x + 12.
Penyelesaian:
a = –1 < 0 → titik maksimum.
b² – 4ac = 4² – 4(–1)(12) = 16 + 48 = 64 > 0 → graf bersilang paksi-x pada dua titik.
Cari verteks: (x – 2)² = x² – 4x + 4, maka f(x) = –(x² – 4x – 12) = –[(x² – 4x + 4) – 4 – 12] = –[(x – 2)² – 16] = –(x – 2)² + 16. Maka verteks (2, 16) dan paksi simetri x = 2.
Cari pintasan-x: –x² + 4x + 12 = 0 → (–x + 6)(x + 2) = 0 → x = 6 atau x = –2.
Cari pintasan-y: f(0) = 12 → (0, 12).
Plot titik-titik: (–2,0), (6,0), (0,12), (2,16). Lukis parabola simetri melalui titik-titik ini.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa: (i) Keliru antara a > 0 (minimum) dan a < 0 (maksimum). (ii) Tidak memfaktorkan atau menyempurnakan kuasa dua dengan betul untuk mencari verteks. (iii) Lupa bahawa diskriminan menentukan bilangan titik persilangan paksi-x, bukan bentuk graf. (iv) Melakar graf tanpa menentukan skala atau simetri.

concept_explanation: Fungsi kuadratik sering digunakan untuk memodelkan situasi dunia sebenar seperti gerakan peluru. Dalam masalah ini, ketinggian lembing diberikan oleh fungsi h(t) = -5t² + 14t + 3. Untuk mencari ketinggian maksimum, tukarkan fungsi ke bentuk verteks h(t) = a(t - h)² + k, di mana nilai k ialah ketinggian maksimum. Untuk mencari masa lembing menyentuh tanah, selesaikan h(t) = 0 (persamaan kuadratik) dan ambil nilai t yang positif.
worked_example: Suresh melempar lembing pada ketinggian 3 meter dari tanah. Fungsi ketinggian lembing ialah h(t) = -5t² + 14t + 3, dengan h ialah tinggi (m) dan t ialah masa (saat). (a) Cari tinggi maksimum lembing. (b) Hitung masa apabila lembing menyentuh tanah. Penyelesaian: (a) Bentuk verteks: h(t) = -5(t² - 2.8t) + 3 = -5[(t - 1.4)² - 1.96] + 3 = -5(t - 1.4)² + 9.8 + 3 = -5(t - 1.4)² + 12.8. Maka tinggi maksimum = 12.8 m. (b) Selesaikan -5t² + 14t + 3 = 0 → 5t² - 14t - 3 = 0 → (5t + 1)(t - 3) = 0 → t = -0.2 (ditolak) atau t = 3. Maka lembing menyentuh tanah pada masa 3 saat.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa termasuk mengambil nilai t negatif sebagai jawapan atau tidak menukarkan fungsi ke bentuk verteks dengan betul.

concept_explanation: Fungsi kuadratik dalam bentuk am f(x) = ax² + bx + c boleh ditulis dalam bentuk verteks f(x) = a(x - h)² + k, dengan (h, k) ialah titik verteks. Nilai maksimum atau minimum fungsi kuadratik berlaku pada verteks: jika a < 0, nilai maksimum adalah k, dan jika a > 0, nilai minimum adalah k. Koordinat verteks boleh dicari dengan formula h = -b/(2a) dan k = f(h). Kaedah melengkapkan kuasa dua juga boleh digunakan untuk mendapatkan bentuk verteks.
worked_example:
Soalan: Fungsi ketinggian lembing h(t) = -5t² + 14t + 3, dengan t ialah masa dalam saat. (a) Cari tinggi maksimum lembing. (b) Bila lembing menyentuh tanah?

Penyelesaian:
(a) Kaedah melengkapkan kuasa dua:
h(t) = -5(t² - 14/5 t) + 3
= -5[t² - 14/5 t + (7/5)² - (7/5)²] + 3
= -5[(t - 7/5)² - 49/25] + 3
= -5(t - 7/5)² + 5(49/25) + 3
= -5(t - 7/5)² + 49/5 + 15/5
= -5(t - 7/5)² + 64/5
Maka verteks (7/5, 64/5). Oleh kerana a = -5 < 0, tinggi maksimum ialah 64/5 = 12.8 m pada t = 1.4 s.

(b) Apabila lembing menyentuh tanah, h(t) = 0:
-5t² + 14t + 3 = 0
5t² - 14t - 3 = 0
(5t + 1)(t - 3) = 0
t = -1/5 (ditolak) atau t = 3
Maka lembing menyentuh tanah selepas 3 saat.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering lupa menolak nilai masa negatif (t = -1/5) dalam masalah aplikasi, atau tersilap tanda semasa melengkapkan kuasa dua, terutamanya apabila pekali a negatif.

subtopic: 3.1 Sistem Persamaan Linear dalam Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_title: Sistem Persamaan Linear dalam Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah terdiri daripada sekurang-kurangnya dua persamaan linear yang mengandungi set pemboleh ubah yang sama, iaitu x, y, dan z. Bentuk am persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah ialah ax + by + cz = d, dengan a, b, dan c tidak semuanya sifar. Setiap persamaan mewakili suatu satah dalam ruang tiga dimensi. Penyelesaian sistem ini adalah titik persilangan ketiga-tiga satah tersebut.
worked_example:
Contoh: Harga satu tiket (x), satu botol minuman (y), dan satu baldi popcorn (z) boleh dimodelkan oleh sistem berikut: 
x + y + 2z = 13
2x + 2y + z = 17
3x + 3y + 2z = 27
Sistem ini perlu diselesaikan untuk mendapatkan nilai x, y, dan z.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering menganggap bahawa tiga persamaan semestinya memberikan satu penyelesaian unik, padahal sistem boleh mempunyai tiada penyelesaian atau penyelesaian tak terhingga jika satah-satah selari atau bertindih.

concept_explanation: A system of linear equations in three variables consists of three equations, each of the form ax + by + cz = d, where a, b, c, and d are constants. Geometrically, each equation represents a plane in three-dimensional space, and the solution is the intersection of these planes. Unlike two-variable systems that form straight lines, three-variable systems form planes. The variables must each be of power 1 for the system to be linear.
worked_example:
Example 1: Determine whether the following are systems of linear equations in three variables.
(a) 2x + 4y – z = 10, x + y = 10z², 5y – z – 2x = 3
(b) p + 8q – 4r = 2, 2(p + 6r) + 7q = 0, 10r + p = 5q
Solution:
(a) No, because the second equation has a variable of power 2 (z²).
(b) Yes, because all three equations have variables p, q, r of power 1 after simplifying.
common_mistakes: Assuming that any equation with three variables is linear, even if variables have exponents other than 1 (e.g., x², y³). Also, forgetting to check if each equation is in the form ax + by + cz = d after simplification.

subtopic: 3.1 Sistem Persamaan Linear dalam Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah terdiri daripada tiga persamaan linear yang masing-masing mengandungi tiga pemboleh ubah (x, y, z). Penyelesaian sistem ini ialah titik persilangan (x, y, z) bagi ketiga-tiga satah yang diwakili oleh persamaan tersebut. Jika ketiga-tiga satah bersilang pada satu titik, maka sistem mempunyai satu penyelesaian unik.
common_mistakes: Pelajar sering keliru bahawa sistem tiga persamaan linear sentiasa mempunyai satu penyelesaian. Sebenarnya, mungkin tiada penyelesaian (satah selari atau tidak bersilang serentak) atau tak terhingga penyelesaian (satah bertindih).

subtopic: Sistem Persamaan Linear dalam Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_title: Jenis Penyelesaian Sistem Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah boleh mempunyai tiga jenis penyelesaian. Pertama, penyelesaian unik berlaku apabila ketiga-tiga satah bersilang pada satu titik. Kedua, penyelesaian tak terhingga berlaku apabila satah-satah bersilang di sepanjang satu garis lurus. Ketiga, tiada penyelesaian berlaku apabila satah-satah tidak bersilang antara satu sama lain. Kaedah untuk menyelesaikan sistem ini termasuk kaedah penghapusan dan kaedah penggantian.
common_mistakes: Menganggap bahawa semua sistem tiga pemboleh ubah mempunyai penyelesaian unik; sebenarnya, terdapat tiga jenis penyelesaian: unik, tak terhingga, dan tiada penyelesaian.

subtopic: Solving Systems of Linear Equations in Three Variables
concept_explanation: The elimination method solves a system of linear equations by eliminating one variable at a time through addition or subtraction of equations, after scaling them to have equal coefficients. For three variables, choose two pairs of equations to eliminate the same variable, reducing the system to two equations in two variables, then solve and back-substitute to find all unknowns.
worked_example:
Solve:
4x – 3y + z = –10
2x + y + 3z = 0
–x + 2y – 5z = 17

Solution:
1. Multiply equation 2 by 2: 4x + 2y + 6z = 0 (3).
2. Subtract (1) from (3): 5y + 5z = 10 → y + z = 2 (4).
3. Multiply equation 3 by 2: –2x + 4y – 10z = 34 (5).
4. Add (2) and (5): 5y – 7z = 34 (6).
5. Subtract (4) multiplied by 5 from (6): (5y – 7z) – 5(y + z) = 34 – 10 → –12z = 24 → z = –2.
6. Substitute z = –2 into (4): y – 2 = 2 → y = 4.
7. Substitute y = 4, z = –2 into (1): 4x – 12 – 2 = –10 → 4x = 4 → x = 1.
Solution: x = 1, y = 4, z = –2.
common_mistakes: Students often forget to multiply every term of an equation when scaling, leading to incorrect coefficients. Another common error is choosing different variables to eliminate in each pair, resulting in an unsolvable system. Always eliminate the same variable from both pairs.

subtopic: 3.1.2 Penyelesaian Sistem Persamaan Linear dalam Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_explanation: Sistem tiga persamaan linear dengan tiga pemboleh ubah boleh diselesaikan menggunakan kaedah penggantian atau penghapusan. Langkah-langkahnya melibatkan menghapuskan satu pemboleh ubah secara berperingkat sehingga memperoleh nilai setiap pemboleh ubah. Jika semasa penghapusan wujud percanggahan seperti 0 = 12, maka sistem itu tidak mempunyai penyelesaian.
worked_example:
Selesaikan sistem persamaan linear berikut.
x – y + 3z = 3 …(1)
–2x + 2y – 6z = 6 …(2)
y – 5z = –3 …(3)
Penyelesaian:
(1) × 2: 2x – 2y + 6z = 6 …(4)
(4) + (2): 0 + 0 + 0 = 12 → 0 = 12
Oleh kerana 0 ≠ 12, sistem ini tidak mempunyai penyelesaian.
common_mistakes: Pelajar tersilap menyimpulkan bahawa 0 = 12 bermaksud sistem mempunyai penyelesaian tak terhingga, sedangkan ia menunjukkan ketiadaan penyelesaian.

concept_title: System of linear equations with infinite solutions
concept_explanation: When solving a system of three linear equations in three variables using the elimination method, if the elimination leads to an identity such as 0 = 0, it indicates that the equations are dependent and the system has infinitely many solutions. This occurs when two or more equations represent the same plane or are linear combinations of each other. The solution set is a line or plane of intersection.
worked_example: Solve: 3x + 5y – 2z = 13, –5x – 2y – 4z = 20, –14x – 17y + 2z = –19. Solution: Multiply first equation by 2: 6x + 10y – 4z = 26. Subtract second equation: (6x+10y-4z) – (-5x-2y-4z) = 26-20 → 11x+12y = 6. Add first and third: (3x+5y-2z)+(-14x-17y+2z) = 13-19 → -11x-12y = -6. Add the two resulting equations: (11x+12y)+(-11x-12y) = 6-6 → 0 = 0. Since 0=0 is true, the system has infinitely many solutions.
common_mistakes: Students often think that obtaining 0=0 means the system has no solution. In fact, 0=0 indicates that the equations are dependent and there are infinitely many solutions.

concept_explanation: A system of three linear equations in three variables can be solved by using elimination and substitution methods. First, eliminate one variable from two pairs of equations to obtain two equations in two variables. Then solve the reduced system using substitution or elimination. The solution is an ordered triple (x, y, z) that satisfies all three equations.
worked_example: Problem: A condominium has three types of units A, B, C. Total daily rent is RM1240. Savings: 10% for A, 20% for B, 30% for C, total savings RM276. Rent of C is twice rent of A. Find each rent. Solution: Let a, b, c be rents. Equations: a+b+c=1240, 0.1a+0.2b+0.3c=276, c=2a. Substitute c=2a into first two, then eliminate b to find a=280, c=560, b=400.
common_mistakes: Students often make sign errors when subtracting equations or forget to multiply all terms when scaling equations.

concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan linear tiga pemboleh ubah (SPLTV) terdiri daripada tiga persamaan linear dengan tiga pemboleh ubah. Untuk menyelesaikan masalah yang melibatkan SPLTV, langkah pertama adalah menterjemahkan situasi ke dalam bentuk persamaan. Kemudian, gunakan kaedah penghapusan atau penggantian untuk mencari nilai setiap pemboleh ubah. Contohnya, jika kos pen dan pensel adalah sama, dan jumlah pen dan pensel sama dengan bilangan buku nota, maka kita boleh membentuk tiga persamaan berdasarkan maklumat tersebut.
worked_example:
Ramasamy ingin membeli pen, pensel dan buku nota dengan RM102. Harga pen = RM5, pensel = RM3, buku nota = RM9. Dia ingin membelanjakan jumlah yang sama untuk pen dan pensel. Jumlah pen dan pensel yang dibeli mestilah sama dengan bilangan buku nota. Berapa banyak setiap item yang akan dibeli? 

Penyelesaian:
Biarkan p = bilangan pen, q = bilangan pensel, r = bilangan buku nota.
Persamaan 1: 5p + 3q + 9r = 102 (jumlah wang)
Persamaan 2: 5p = 3q (perbelanjaan sama untuk pen dan pensel)
Persamaan 3: p + q = r (bilangan pen + pensel = bilangan buku nota)

Dari persamaan 2, q = (5/3)p. Gantikan ke persamaan 3: p + (5/3)p = r → (8/3)p = r. Gantikan ke persamaan 1: 5p + 3(5/3)p + 9(8/3)p = 102 → 5p + 5p + 24p = 102 → 34p = 102 → p = 3. Maka q = 5, r = 8. Jadi, Ramasamy membeli 3 pen, 5 pensel dan 8 buku nota.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa adalah salah menterjemahkan ayat seperti 'jumlah yang sama' menjadi persamaan yang tidak tepat. Pastikan anda menggunakan pemboleh ubah yang konsisten dan menyemak semula setiap persamaan dengan situasi asal.

subtopic: 3.2 Simultanius Persamaan Melibatkan Satu Persamaan Linear dan Satu Persamaan Tak Linear
concept_title: Simultanius Persamaan Linear dan Tak Linear
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan simultan ini terdiri daripada dua persamaan dengan dua pemboleh ubah, di mana satu persamaan adalah linear dan satu lagi adalah tak linear (seperti kuadratik). Kaedah penyelesaian utama adalah penggantian: ungkapkan satu pemboleh ubah daripada persamaan linear dan gantikan ke dalam persamaan tak linear. Ini menghasilkan satu persamaan dalam satu pemboleh ubah yang boleh diselesaikan. Contoh situasi termasuk perimeter dan luas segi empat tepat, atau hasil tambah dan hasil darab dua nombor.
common_mistakes: PELAJAR sering keliru antara persamaan linear dan tak linear, atau gagal mengenal pasti bahawa persamaan tak linear mungkin berbentuk kuadratik, kubik, atau lain-lain. Juga, kesilapan dalam proses penggantian atau penyelesaian persamaan kuadratik boleh berlaku.

subtopic: Penyelesaian Persamaan Serentak Linear dan Tak Linear
concept_explanation: Persamaan serentak terdiri daripada satu persamaan linear dan satu persamaan tak linear. Untuk menyelesaikannya dengan kaedah penggantian, ungkapkan satu pemboleh ubah daripada persamaan linear, kemudian gantikan ke dalam persamaan tak linear. Ini menghasilkan persamaan kuadratik yang boleh diselesaikan melalui pemfaktoran atau formula. Penyelesaian akhir diperoleh dengan menggantikan nilai tersebut semula ke dalam persamaan linear untuk mendapatkan nilai pemboleh ubah yang lain. Titik-titik persilangan antara kedua-dua graf adalah penyelesaian persamaan serentak.
worked_example:
Selesaikan persamaan serentak: 2x + y = 4 dan y^2 + 5 = 4x dengan kaedah penggantian.
Penyelesaian:
Dari 2x + y = 4, ungkapkan x = (4 - y)/2.
Gantikan ke dalam y^2 + 5 = 4x: y^2 + 5 = 4[(4 - y)/2] = 8 - 2y.
Maka y^2 + 2y - 3 = 0 → (y + 3)(y - 1) = 0 → y = -3 atau y = 1.
Gantikan y ke dalam x = (4 - y)/2:
Apabila y = -3, x = (4 - (-3))/2 = 7/2 = 3.5.
Apabila y = 1, x = (4 - 1)/2 = 3/2 = 1.5.
Penyelesaian: (x, y) = (3.5, -3) dan (1.5, 1).
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa termasuk tidak menggantikan kembali ke dalam persamaan linear untuk mendapatkan nilai pemboleh ubah yang lain, atau melakukan kesilapan algebra semasa mengembangkan dan memudahkan persamaan kuadratik. Juga, kadangkala pelajar lupa bahawa terdapat dua penyelesaian untuk y dan seterusnya dua pasangan penyelesaian.

concept_explanation: Simultaneous equations involving one linear and one quadratic equation can be solved using elimination or graphical methods. The elimination method involves aligning terms and adding or subtracting to eliminate one variable, resulting in a quadratic equation that is then solved using the quadratic formula. The graphical method requires plotting points for both equations and finding their intersection points, which represent the solutions.
worked_example:
Example 8: Solve 2x + y = 4 and x² – 2xy = 3 using elimination.
Solution:
2x + y = 4 …①
x² – 2xy = 3 …②
Multiply ① by 2x: 4x² + 2xy = 8x …③
Add ② and ③: 5x² = 3 + 8x → 5x² – 8x – 3 = 0
Use quadratic formula: x = [8 ± √(64 + 60)]/(10) = [8 ± √124]/10
x = 1.9136 or x = –0.3136
Substitute into ①:
For x = 1.9136: y = 4 – 2(1.9136) = 0.1728
For x = –0.3136: y = 4 – 2(–0.3136) = 4.6272
Thus solutions: (1.9136, 0.1728) and (–0.3136, 4.6272).
common_mistakes: Students may forget to substitute both x values back to find the corresponding y values, or they may incorrectly multiply equations leading to sign errors.

concept_explanation: Menyelesaikan persamaan serentak secara graf melibatkan melukis graf bagi kedua-dua persamaan pada paksi yang sama. Titik persilangan graf mewakili penyelesaian kepada sistem persamaan. Bagi persamaan serentak yang melibatkan satu persamaan linear dan satu persamaan tak linear, mungkin terdapat sehingga dua titik persilangan. Contohnya, persamaan y² – 4x = 0 dan 2x + y = 4 menghasilkan dua penyelesaian: (1,2) dan (4,–4).
worked_example: Selesaikan persamaan serentak y² – 4x = 0 dan 2x + y = 4 secara graf. Daripada graf, terdapat dua titik persilangan iaitu (1,2) dan (4,–4). Oleh itu, penyelesaian ialah x=1, y=2 dan x=4, y=–4.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa ialah hanya membaca satu titik persilangan atau salah membaca graf akibat skala yang tidak tepat. Sentiasa semak kedua-dua titik dengan menggantikan ke dalam kedua-dua persamaan asal.

concept_title: Applying simultaneous equations to geometry problems
concept_explanation: In geometry problems, we often form a system of simultaneous equations from given conditions: one non-linear equation (e.g., from Pythagoras theorem for lengths) and one linear equation (e.g., from total perimeter). Solving the system yields unknown dimensions, which can then be used to compute quantities like volume. The solution must satisfy all constraints and be physically meaningful.
worked_example: Example: A right prism with a square base has total side length 133 cm, and ED = BC = 25 cm. Can a piece of dodol of volume 600 cm³ be packed? Let base side = x cm and height = y cm. Equations: x² + y² = 25² (from BC length using Pythagoras) and 5x + 2y + 50 = 133 (total side length). Simplify linear: 5x + 2y = 83 → y = (83 - 5x)/2. Substitute into non-linear: x² + [(83 - 5x)/2]² = 625 → 29x² - 830x + 4389 = 0 → (29x - 627)(x - 7) = 0 → x = 627/29 (≈21.62) or x = 7. For x = 7, y = (83 - 35)/2 = 24; volume = 7² × 24 = 1176 cm³ > 600 cm³. For x = 627/29, y ≈ (83 - 108.1)/2 negative → not valid. Thus, container volume (1176 cm³) exceeds 600 cm³, so the dodol can be packed.
common_mistakes: Common mistakes include incorrectly forming the equations (e.g., omitting the 50 cm for the extra sides), forgetting to verify that solutions yield positive dimensions, or not checking which solution is physically plausible.

concept_explanation: Simultaneous equations involve two or more equations that are solved together to find common variables. In SPM, you often solve linear equations with quadratic equations using substitution. For practical problems, form equations from given conditions like area and perimeter, then solve for unknowns. Always check solutions in original equations.
worked_example:
Example: A rectangular plank has area 72 cm² and perimeter 34 cm. Find length (l) and width (w).
Equations: lw = 72, 2(l+w) = 34 → l+w = 17.
Substitute w = 17 - l into lw = 72: l(17 - l) = 72 → 17l - l² = 72 → l² - 17l + 72 = 0 → (l - 8)(l - 9) = 0 → l = 8 or 9.
If l = 8, w = 9; if l = 9, w = 8. So length = 9 cm, width = 8 cm (or vice versa).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to check which solution is valid in context; mixing up substitution steps; not simplifying equations correctly.

concept_title: Sistem Persamaan Linear dan Tak Linear
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan terdiri daripada persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah atau gabungan satu persamaan linear dan satu persamaan tak linear. Kaedah penyelesaian termasuk penghapusan, penggantian, dan kaedah graf. Sistem boleh mempunyai satu penyelesaian, tiada penyelesaian, atau penyelesaian tak terhingga. Pemahaman tentang hubungan antara pemboleh ubah adalah penting untuk memodel dan menyelesaikan masalah harian.

concept_title: Sistem Persamaan Linear Tiga Pemboleh Ubah
concept_explanation: Sistem persamaan linear dalam tiga pemboleh ubah terdiri daripada tiga persamaan linear dengan tiga anu (x, y, z). Penyelesaian sistem ini adalah nilai x, y, dan z yang memenuhi ketiga-tiga persamaan serentak. Kaedah penghapusan atau penggantian boleh digunakan untuk mencari penyelesaian ini, dengan kaedah penghapusan melibatkan penambahan atau penolakan persamaan untuk menghapuskan satu pemboleh ubah.
common_mistakes: Kesilapan biasa adalah tidak menyemak penyelesaian dengan menggantikan nilai ke dalam semua persamaan asal, atau membuat kesilapan aritmetik semasa proses penghapusan.

subtopic: Menyelesaikan Masalah yang Melibatkan Sistem Persamaan Linear Serentak
concept_explanation: Bagi masalah yang melibatkan luas dan perimeter, dua persamaan linear serentak boleh dibentuk dengan menggunakan pemboleh ubah bagi panjang dan lebar. Contohnya, jika karpet mempunyai luas 8.75 m² dan perimeter 12 m, maka persamaan luas: p × l = 8.75 dan persamaan perimeter: 2(p + l) = 12. Sistem persamaan ini boleh diselesaikan dengan kaedah penghapusan atau penggantian untuk mencari nilai panjang dan lebar karpet. Seterusnya, panjang dan lebar bilik diperoleh dengan menambah jarak dari dinding.
worked_example:
Soalan 9: Rajah menunjukkan pelan bilik segi empat tepat. Karpet segi empat tepat diletakkan dengan jarak 1 m dari dinding bilik. Luas karpet = 8.75 m², perimeter karpet = 12 m. Cari panjang dan lebar bilik.
Penyelesaian:
Katakan panjang karpet = x m, lebar karpet = y m.
Luas: xy = 8.75
Perimeter: 2(x + y) = 12 → x + y = 6
Maka, x dan y adalah punca bagi persamaan kuadratik: t² - 6t + 8.75 = 0.
Selesaikan: (t - 2.5)(t - 3.5) = 0 → t = 2.5 atau t = 3.5.
Jadi, karpet berukuran 2.5 m × 3.5 m (atau sebaliknya).
Bilik mempunyai jarak 1 m dari setiap dinding, maka panjang bilik = 2.5 + 2(1) = 4.5 m, lebar bilik = 3.5 + 2(1) = 5.5 m. (Atau sebaliknya bergantung orientasi).
common_mistakes: Tidak menambah jarak dari dinding dengan betul. Pelajar mungkin lupa menambah 2 m (1 m setiap sisi) pada panjang dan lebar karpet untuk mendapatkan dimensi bilik.

concept_explanation: This chapter introduces the laws of indices, surds, and logarithms, which are fundamental tools in algebra. Students will learn to apply these laws to simplify expressions and solve equations. Key definitions include index (the exponent of a base), surd (an irrational number expressed with a radical sign), and logarithm (the inverse operation of exponentiation). The chapter also covers conjugate surds and natural logarithms.
